subject: Planned node sanitization sweep — staggered drain & minimal-impact window
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: ops-eng@acmeai.com, platform-contact@globex.ai, support@starlight.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Planned node sanitization sweep — staggered drain & minimal-impact window

Hi all,

We want to let you know about a planned maintenance activity in the US region next week that affects inference nodes serving the Redwood Hosted API. This is a proactive "node sanitization" sweep: a coordinated sequence of kernel/driver micro-updates and a light reprobe of device firmware to address a class of long-running stability issues we've observed in a small subset of backplane controllers.

High level:
- Maintenance window: 2026-08-12 01:00–06:00 UTC (staggered across availability clusters).
- Expected customer-facing impact: brief (typically 20–120s) warm handoffs or short tail latency spikes while individual nodes are drained and restarted. We will proceed one rack at a time to avoid region-wide disruption.
- Rollout approach: canary cluster in us-east-1 -> trailing clusters in us-east-2/us-central with pause points and health gates.
- Safety: automatic fallback to compatible model variant and routing to warm standby capacity if a node does not return within SLO.
- KV cache & session continuity: we will attempt KV cache preservation via live handoff where supported; transient cache misses may occur for long-running chat sessions.

Action requested from customers:
1) If you have scheduled high-throughput jobs within the window above, please let us know your job identifiers so we can avoid handoffs mid-run.
2) Confirm whether you require an extended quiet window for a particular cluster (we can schedule a dedicated canary outside the primary window for critical tenants).

Attachments: maintenance-plan-20260807.pdf (overview timeline, rollback & validation steps), hotfix-checklist-ava-20260807.xlsx (internal run checklist).

We will publish a live progress page and update customers as the canary completes. If you prefer us to route your traffic to Dedicated capacity for the maintenance period, reply and we'll provide a short-term plan.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Sr. Product Ops — North America
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Huang <ops-eng@acmeai.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned node sanitization sweep — staggered drain & minimal-impact window

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the heads up. Two quick questions from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the KV cache handoff is supported for long-running streaming sessions (we have a handful of conversations that exceed 20k tokens)?
- If a node is drained mid-inference, do you preserve the model shard affinity so requests go back to the same warmed model shard after the handoff, or do we risk higher cold-start token costs for a short period?

We are planning a low-traffic batch for 2026-08-12 02:30 UTC but have a customer demo at 03:45 UTC — if there's any risk to the demo we'd prefer to request an exemption for our cluster.

Regards,
Sam Huang
Platform SRE, Acme AI

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planned node sanitization sweep — staggered drain & minimal-impact window

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick questions, good ones. Short answers below, plus details and links.

1) KV cache & streaming sessions:
We will attempt in-memory KV handoff for streaming sessions where the runtime has an active warm peer in the canary cluster. For very long sessions (20k+ tokens) there are two caveats:
- If the session is pinned to a node with a proprietary driver state that cannot be transferred, you may see a short re-warm (order of seconds) while the session state is reconstructed from persisted checkpoints.
- We will not force session termination; the platform will prefer live handoff where possible.

2) Model shard affinity & cold-start token costs:
Our routing preserves shard affinity when a node comes back online in the same cluster. However, during the brief handoff window some requests may be routed to adjacent shards or standby variants which can cause a short increase in cold-token operations. We expect this to be bounded and visible in the token-level telemetry that we'll publish.

If you need an exclusion for your demo window (03:45 UTC), we can schedule the canary to avoid your cluster or set an explicit hold — please reply with the cluster name or your account id and we'll mark it.

For more detail, see the runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/maintenance-runbooks/AVASWP and the incident ticket INF-3421.

I'll loop in Marissa and Jordan to coordinate a canary exclusion if needed.

Thanks,
Ava
